---
title: "Grade reports as pairwise decisions"
subtitle: "2.2 · block reading after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), slide 56"
description: "Pairwise statements induced by assigning units to ordered grades."
---

Assigning sites to ordered grades states a direction for every pair in different grades and withholds every pair sharing a grade — without claiming shared-grade sites are equal.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/report-builder.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["report-builder"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **A, then B to E, then F.** States 9 of the 15 pairs (share .600) and withholds 6 inside the four-site middle grade.
- **Three grades of two sites.** Three grades now state 12 of the 15 pairs (share .800) and withhold 3, showing how grade sizes govern disclosure.
- **Four sites: 1/2/2/2.** States 3 of the 6 pairs (share .500). Focus a site and press a grade number, or press Enter, use Up/Down/Home/End, and press Enter to place it.
- **Beyond letter order.** The report {B, D} > {C, F} > {A, E} also states 12 of the 15 pairs; mirrored cells represent one unordered pair.

<details>
<summary>Context and scope notes</summary>

In this example, an evaluation office plans practice-documentation visits to fictional after-school sites. The grades carry no funding consequence. The exercise counts the directions in the report the reader supplies; it does not use posterior probabilities to judge whether those directions are likely to be right. When a move empties a grade, the remaining grades keep their relative order.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
postrank_evaluate(c(A=1L,B=1L,C=2L,D=2L,E=3L,F=3L), pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$N # 12
canonical_postrank_grade(c(A=3L,B=3L,C=7L,D=7L,E=9L,F=9L), LETTERS[1:6]) # 1 1 2 2 3 3
```
:::

Standalone: [report builder](../../embed/report-builder.html), for example `?units=6&grades=3,1,2,1,3,2`.
